title: consumer/1: how one Consumer repo is served (design section 3.12). A data file: its path is its identity and the commit its Release. Its protected paths are in the one syntax of config/hooks.json, read alike by the Kernel's matcher (kernel/derive.py, matches) and the session hooks' (tools/hooks/protected.py, entries); and they name its setup and test scripts, which tools/check_examples.py holds. What reads an entry, the readiness check and apply's refusal for a Consumer repo, is slice 3's.

ring.description: The Channel that serves the repo, as release/rings.json names it.

ci_workflows.description: The name of each of the repo's own workflows whose checks the Factory reads, as GitHub shows it.

setup.description: The repo's setup script, by its path from the top of the repo.

test.description: The repo's test script, by its path from the top of the repo.

protected_paths.description: What apply refuses a Role's push to without a person (slice 3's): relative to the top of the repo; a path ending in / is a directory and all below it; * stands for any part of one name; ** as a whole name for any run of names, which both matchers read, as a rubric's paths use it (decision 0029), though config/hooks.json itself names none; case is ignored (issue 141, decision 0020). Its setup and test scripts are among them.

reviewers.description: The repo's Advisory reviewers, by the name the Factory gives each, one at least: adopting the Factory needs them configured (design section 3.12).
